For review — Adrian · 22 October 2026

Heading font — seven options on the real screens

Only the heading font changes: page titles, card titles and the case heading. Sizes, weights (600), colours and everything else are exactly as they are in the app today, and the body text stays Inter throughout. These are screenshots of the real app (local copy, demo data), not drawings.

Side by side — Discussions

Our view

  • To keep a serif, as the style guide intended ("the authority of an institution"), Source Serif 4 is the closest swap: the same editorial register as Fraunces without the decorative quirks that make it feel out of place.
  • To go all-sans, Inter (headings in the body font) is the cleanest and most consistent; Public Sans gives a slightly more institutional, public-health feel.
  • Any choice is a one-line change to a design token plus the font file. All seven are open-licensed (SIL OFL) and would be self-hosted like the current fonts, so nothing is fetched from Google at runtime. A sans choice also means updating the style guide, which currently specifies a serif for headings.

1. Fraunces Serif · today

The current heading font. A characterful, "soft" serif with quirky details (the curled terminals on a, g and y); this is what reads as slightly out of place beside the clean, clinical Inter.

2. Source Serif 4 Serif

Adobe's text serif, designed to sit beside a sans. Calm, upright and professional — keeps the editorial serif register the style guide asked for, without Fraunces's personality. The closest like-for-like swap.

3. Newsreader Serif

A newspaper serif with a narrower, more condensed feel. Reads as journal-like, which suits a literature feed; titles take slightly less width.

4. Inter Sans · same as the body text

No separate heading font: headings in the body font at the same weight. The most consistent and modern option — the hierarchy then comes entirely from size and weight.

5. Plus Jakarta Sans Sans

A geometric sans with a little warmth. Friendlier and more "product" than Inter, while still clearly different from the body text.

6. Manrope Sans

A semi-condensed modern sans; tidy and technical. Fits more of a long title on one line.

7. Public Sans Sans

Built for government services (US Web Design System), neutral and very legible. Has the institutional, public-health feel of NHS-style interfaces.
